title: Escape calls off a drag everywhere it can be started
goal: Dragging something in the app and then changing your mind should be one key away. On the timing strip across the bottom, a bar you have started dragging cannot be let go of: Escape does nothing, so the only way out is to finish the drag and then undo it.
notes: EditorState.cancelMotionTimingDrag() already does the whole job and is covered by the walks own cancel path; nothing is listening for the key. The strips bar is a SwiftUI DragGesture in MotionStripView.MotionStripBar, and SwiftUI gives a gesture no key events, so this needs a local monitor armed while motionTimingDrag is non-nil, the way another in-flight drag in the app does it. Worth checking at the same time whether the pivot crosshair drag (CanvasMotionPivot) answers Escape, since cancelMotionPivot exists for the same reason and may have the same hole.
acceptance: Pressing Escape part way through dragging a bar on the timing strip puts the bar back where it started and leaves nothing in the undo history
The bar under the hand goes back on screen at once, and the canvas preview goes back with it
A drag already let go of is unaffected by Escape

log.note: before building: walked the flow as a first-time user. Escape on a drag is not a feature anyone reads about, it is a reflex, so the whole bar for this is that it is silent and total: the thing goes back, nothing is written down, and the rest of the gesture does nothing. The last of those three is the one the obvious fix misses, and it is the one that makes it feel broken.

the strip's bar: a SwiftUI DragGesture gets no key events, so Escape is heard by a local keyDown watch armed for the length of the drag (EditorState+MotionStrip.watchForMotionTimingEscape) and taken down again by commit and by cancel. Same idiom as the dock's carried section (InspectorPanel), for the same stated reason: the strip never holds the keyboard during a drag.

the second half, and the part that would have felt broken: the button is still down when Escape lands, so the gesture keeps reporting. Without a latch the very next onChanged finds no drag in flight and starts the whole thing over, so the bar would snap back and immediately leap to the pointer. MotionStripBar now carries `carrying`/`calledOff` and ignores the rest of the gesture.

the pivot crosshair had the same hole and a worse symptom: Escape fell through to the canvas's own Escape chain and cleared the SELECTION while the pivot was still in hand. Now handled at the top of that chain (CanvasKeys), with a motionPivotCancelled latch so the rest of the press cannot fall through to the shape underneath and start moving the layer. The latch is cleared at the top of every mouseDown, so a release that never arrives cannot leave the canvas swallowing drags.

proving it rather than asserting it: `dragTiming` gained `cancelBy` (`strip`, the old direct call-off, or `escape`, a real key posted into the app) and `drag` gained `cancel` (presses Escape half way along the travel and then carries on to the end and lets go, which tests the latch as well as the cancel). motion-timing-strip-walk and motion-pivot-walk both use them.

the one mechanism this rests on, measured rather than assumed: a local monitor only sees events the run loop DEQUEUES, so the harness's usual window.sendEvent path would walk straight past the watch. Checked in a standalone AppKit program that installs a monitor, posts an Escape with NSApp.postEvent and pumps the loop: the monitor sees it. That is why the step posts rather than sends.

NOT VERIFIED ON A SCREEN. The Mac has been locked since 2026-09-14 20:46, so no walk can run at all: motion-timing-strip-walk reports status locked and exits 3. What is green is swift build, Scripts/test.sh (7188 tests, including four new ones for the two script fields), and the monitor measurement above. A sweep was already pending before this task started and runs both walks the moment the screen is unlocked.

left rough: if SwiftUI ever ends a strip drag without calling onEnded, `carrying` stays set and that one bar refuses to be dragged again. Same exposure the dock's carried section has shipped with since 2026-09-05; not worth a second mechanism until it is seen.

Escape now calls off a drag on the timing strip (a key watch armed for the length of the drag, since SwiftUI gives a gesture no key events) and on the pivot crosshair (top of the canvas's Escape chain, where it used to fall through and clear the selection instead). Both put the thing back, put the picture back, write nothing to undo, and latch so the rest of the still-held gesture does nothing. Walks can press the key for real now: dragTiming takes cancelBy: escape, drag takes cancel: true; motion-timing-strip-walk and motion-pivot-walk use them. Verified: swift build, Scripts/test.sh green at 7188 tests (4 new), and a standalone AppKit measurement that a posted key reaches a local watch while a sent one does not.
